findings.title: No retry on 401 removes the cookie re-read after AccountProvider clears a stale Bearer/impersonation token
findings.body:
The engine authenticates with only the Bearer token when one is present (`engine/api/src/platform/auth/platform-auth.service.ts:1833-1843`: `resolveActorFromRequestToken` checks cookies only when there is no token, and does not fall back to the cookie after a token failure). On a 401, `AccountProvider` (`console/contexts/account-context.tsx:51-58`) calls `unsetToken()` / `unsetImpersonationToken()` but does not call `mutate()`. Before this change, SWR's default retry ran `GET /account` again a few seconds later without the Bearer header, so a valid BetterAuth cookie returned 200 and the person was signed in again. `shouldRetryOnError: (error) => error.status !== 401` removes that re-read.

Failure case: an impersonation token lives 24 h in localStorage (`expiresIn = 86400`, set by `routes/Admin/PlatformUsers/Detail.tsx:165` and `JobsManagement.tsx:88`). An operator with a valid cookie session and an expired impersonation token opens a public `resolveAccount` page (`/offers/*/*`, `/offers/.../start`, `/start`, `/agreements/*`). The first `/account` returns 401, the token is cleared, and nothing re-reads. The operator stays signed out on that page until the next focus, reconnect or reload: `OfferSiteHeader` shows "Log in" and the Start page shows the sign-in/visitor state instead of their Start. Private routes are not affected because `RouteAuthBoundary` already redirects on the first 401. Reviewers differ on impact: one rates it a regression for a live session (major), the other limits it to internal operators who recover on any focus (minor).
findings.fix: In the 401 branch of the `AccountProvider` effect, call `mutate()` once when `unsetToken`/`unsetImpersonationToken` actually removed an existing token, so the cookie-only re-read still happens; keep the no-retry rule for a visitor without a token.
